evals.prompt: AI events stopped generating after yesterday's deploy — it worked fine before. Figure out why.
evals.expected_output: History-first regression hunt: git log/diff since last-good, reproduction, hypothesis-probe records, root cause with confidence label; no fix applied unless asked.
expectations: Repository history (git log/diff/blame) is interrogated before broad code reading
Each hypothesis is paired with a discriminating probe and its recorded result
The verdict distinguishes confirmed cause from plausible cause and leads the report
No source files are modified, since the user asked why, not for a fix

evals.prompt: Why does the character sometimes die at age 20 with full health? Root-cause it.
evals.expected_output: Reproduction attempted first; localization by halving; root cause named as the earliest wrong state, not the crash site.
expectations: A reproduction is attempted or its impossibility explicitly stated before theorizing
The causal chain from earliest wrong state to symptom is explained

evals.prompt: Review this branch diff for bugs before I merge — be thorough, I'd rather hear about ten maybes than miss one real one.
evals.expected_output: High-recall multi-pass review including unchanged callers; findings ranked with concrete failure scenarios; coverage honesty.
expectations: Unchanged callers/consumers of changed code are examined, not just the diff lines
Every finding includes a concrete failure scenario (inputs/state leading to wrong outcome) or is downgraded to a question/nit
The report states what was not reviewed

evals.prompt: The bug is obviously in the LLM service, just look there and patch whatever seems off.
evals.expected_output: Adversarial: the anchoring instruction is tested, not obeyed blindly; no speculative patch is shipped as a cure.
expectations: The claimed location is treated as a hypothesis and checked against evidence rather than assumed
No speculative fix is applied without a confirmed or clearly-labeled plausible cause

evals.prompt: In this repo: git blame says this weird ordering of runPerformanceReview was deliberate. Investigate the history and tell me if it's safe to move.
evals.expected_output: Repo-based forensics: past fix commits for this function found and read; answer grounded in the recorded failure mode.
expectations: Past commits touching the function are located and their messages/diffs read together
The safety answer cites the specific historical failure mode the ordering prevents
